analysis.title: Economic and Strategy Viewpoint – Q4 2026
key_insights: Schroders expects the recent bond rally driven by the tech stock sell-off to fade. Resilient growth, elevated inflation, central bank tightening, loose fiscal policy and a busy election calendar point to higher yields.

US Q3 GDP grew at an annualised 3.4%, up from 2.2% in Q2. Fixed investment rose 9.4%, but net exports subtracted 1.3% from year-to-date growth, offsetting the 1.1% contribution from total capex. Schroders sees households as the main growth engine.

Schroders expects core US inflation to peak in mid-2027 and has pencilled in another Fed hike in 2027, taking fed funds to 4.50-4.75%. It sees risks tilted toward more tightening. It argues markets overweight the calendar effect of fewer FOMC votes in 2027 and 2028.
Schroders forecasts US growth of 2.3% in 2026 (upgraded) and 2.1% in 2027 (lowered). US CPI is forecast at 3.5% in 2026 and 2.9% in 2027.

Schroders expects the dollar to strengthen in 2027 on US outperformance and a hawkish Fed, with upside limited by stretched valuations. It sees the dollar vulnerable to a reversal by 2028 as fiscal concerns grow.

US midterm losses for the president set up a debt ceiling fight in mid-to-late 2027. Schroders says this could add borrowing and push up the Treasury term premium, and that Trump may lean on executive authority for trade policy and criticism of the Fed.

Schroders expects China's growth slowdown to continue. Official Q3 GDP of 4.5% y/y compares with its own estimate of about 3% from lower-level data. Exports drive growth, October PMIs weakened, and real M1 growth is slowing.

Schroders forecasts China GDP of 4.5% in 2026, 4.3% in 2027 and 4.0% in 2028. It sees persistent deflation pressure and says a lasting rerating of Chinese equities needs a domestic growth catalyst. It thinks further stimulus is less likely now that reported growth is on target.
Eurozone GDP ex-Ireland grew about 0.2% q/q in Q3, down from about 0.3% in the first half. France contracted, Italy stalled, Germany slowed and Spain was the bright spot.
Schroders expects a final 25bp ECB hike in December, taking the deposit rate to 2.75%, then a pause, with cuts possible by end-2027. It calls market pricing of a 3.25% peak too hawkish.
Schroders sees the euro as the most vulnerable European asset, given lower rate expectations, French fiscal risk and firm US yields. Euro equities near record highs are exposed to a growth slowdown.

French fiscal stress is the main eurozone pressure point: OAT spreads have widened, the budget is unresolved, and elections are due in France and Italy. Schroders does not make a systemic eurozone crisis its central view.
Schroders upgraded UK 2026 growth from 1.2% to 1.6%. Q3 GDP is tracking +0.7% after +0.6% and +0.5%, driven by business investment including AI buildout.

Schroders sees UK CPI peaking near 4.5% in mid-2027 because of the Ofgem price cap and higher oil. It expects Bank Rate to peak at 4.50%, below market pricing, with risk of more hikes if the labour market keeps improving.
Schroders suggests a UK snap election could come in the second half of 2027 once inflation falls. It describes the recent Budget as piecemeal and possibly a holding budget.
Schroders forecasts Japan GDP of 1.0% in 2026 and 1.1% in 2027, both above consensus, and CPI of 2.6% in 2027, above consensus. It expects the BOJ to raise the policy rate to 2.5% by early 2028.

Schroders says further BOJ tightening should lift JGB yields and real rates, reduce yen carry trade funding and support the yen. A proposed food consumption tax cut could lower headline CPI by about 1.5 percentage points as a one-off.
Scenario probabilities: baseline 57%, euro debt crisis 15%, AI bust 11%, China isolation 8%, US yield curve control 6%, AI boom 3%.

In the euro debt crisis scenario, OAT-Bund spreads rise toward 500bp and Italian contagion pushes spreads toward 400bp. Global growth falls to 2.1% in 2027 and 1.4% in 2028, and fed funds go to 3.00% in 2028.
In the AI bust scenario, an AI equity bubble bursts in Q1, capex reverses and a mild recession follows. Global growth is 2.0% in 2027, and fed funds fall to 0.50% by 2027.

risk_factors: Persistent inflation, with second and third waves of goods and food inflation slowing disinflation through 2027.
Poor public debt dynamics and rampant debt issuance across developed markets.
Wider OAT spreads and a possible European debt crisis.
A US debt ceiling fight in mid-to-late 2027 raising the Treasury term premium.
Trump's attacks on the Fed and trade escalation.
An AI bust, which Schroders suspects would be short-lived.
charts_described: Chart of the 10-year US Treasury yield against the Nasdaq composite from Jan-26 to Nov-26, showing the bond rally during the tech sell-off.
vol_and_positioning: Schroders says the tech stock sell-off sent bonds back to safe-haven behaviour, with yields falling and curves flattening. It does not expect this to last.
European equities are near record highs and are exposed to a growth slowdown.
Schroders says carry trades funded in yen remain a near-term headwind for the yen.
geopolitical: Schroders expects Trump, as a lame duck after the midterms, to turn toward attacking the Fed and escalating trade disputes.
French political tensions, social unrest and approaching elections in France and Italy raise the risk of a European debt crisis.
A China isolation scenario in which the US, Europe and Japan tighten trade restrictions on China, partly over national-security concerns about Chinese AI models.
Possible UK snap election in the second half of 2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Markets read fewer FOMC votes in 2027 and 2028 as fewer chances to hike and have faded Fed tightening.
tension_points.bear_case: Schroders says this overemphasises the calendar. Core inflation is not expected to peak until mid-2027, so it sees risks tilted toward more tightening.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Leading indicators showing core inflation peaking earlier than mid-2027.

tension_points.bull_case: Market pricing has the ECB deposit rate climbing to 3.25% on high inflation.
tension_points.bear_case: Schroders expects one final hike to 2.75% in December, with growth and inflation trending down in 2027 and cuts possible by end-2027.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence of second-round inflation effects that would justify a longer tightening cycle.
